assay_capability_requirement: the frozen readout's margin on the confirmation set >= 0.02 for particle2 in >= 3 of 8 seeds (rows below are marked uninformative)
claim_ceiling: an executable hypothesis for particle2 at d=2 on this catalogue; n=8 seeds
crn_policy: per seed one partition and reset root shared by every genome; permutation for the coincidence probe drawn once per seed
falsification_condition: if neither flag_local_storage nor flag_routed holds in >= 3/4 seeds for particle2, the mechanism is not one of the two named classes (reported as such); flag_coincidence in >= 3/4 seeds kills the 'computation' reading
kill_condition: margin < 0.02 in > 1 seed for particle2 (assay uninformative)
parent_evidence: C2-SFE-09 (n=4): particle2 0.54-0.61 vs random 0.50; not a reset artifact (reset-only < chance), not a dynamical bias (time shuffle removes it), input-dependent; LOCALIZED with k50 = 1 in 11/12 rows.
positive_control: the full single-site lesion drop reproduces campaign 2's localization (site_drop >= 0.5 x margin)
primary_observable: per genome x seed: site s*, phase t*, self_tm1_drop vs neighbour_set_tm1_drop (storage vs routing), site-alone readout with and without reset permutation (coincidence), minimum causal lesion, recovery after refit; primary: particle2 - GKL on site_drop_share_of_margin (are the two mechanisms equally localized?)
question: Which site and time step of particle2 carry its delayed-recall (d=2) margin, and does that site STORE the delayed bit (clamping it one step earlier removes the margin) or EXPOSE information computed by its radius-3 predecessors (clamping them one step earlier removes it)? Same probes on particle1 and GKL.

title: CA mechanism, not usefulness
why_this_slot: Usefulness has been measured twice; the campaign asks for one evolved computational effect reduced to a falsifiable local mechanism, and the single-site localization makes this the cheapest such reduction available.
